newsitem.title: GERMANY: Analysts say German economic recovery is intact.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say German economic recovery is intact.

text.p: Germany continued its export-led recovery in the third quarter, the Economics Ministry said on Wednesday, and analysts said they expected final quarter-on-quarter growth to come out at up to one percent.

The ministry said third quarter growth was likely to be a real two percent year-on-year after 1.2 percent in the second quarter. It said third quarter gross domestic product "clearly rose" after a jump of 1.5 percent in the second quarter.

"We had an extremely high growth rate in the second quarter compared with the previous quarter - mainly because of a catch-up effect after the harsh winter," said Adolf Rosenstock at the Industrial Bank of Japan in Frankfurt. "This could not be repeated in the third quarter."
Rosenstock said he expected quarter-on-quarter growth of between 0.75 and 1.0 percent in the third quarter, meaning that "the upswing is clearly intact."

But analysts expressed concern the government was making its growth estimate so soon after the release of weak September industrial output and orders data which are due for revision. No September retail data have yet been published.

"Second quarter growth was very high at 1.5 percent, and they don't expect that to be revised. If we assume that is right then it would be normal to have one percent growth in the third quarter," said Norbert Braems of BZW in Frankfurt.

Braems said that if there is no significant weakening of economic activity in the fourth quarter, the annual growth rate could come close to 1.5 percent -- but he noted the recovery was narrow and mainly driven by exports.
